cases.rationale: Exact edition, rigid-to-rigid single-lap geometry and tensile lap-shear endpoint.
ISO 4587 explicitly says the procedure does not provide design information.
A short-term lap-shear observation is not a service-life estimate.
D1002-26 identifies its use as primarily comparative for metal-to-metal single-lap specimens.
D1002-26 scope is metal-to-metal, not polymer-to-polymer.
D1002-26 explicitly warns against using its apparent shear result as a design-allowable stress.
D3762-24 supports qualitative wedge-test surface-durability discrimination and failure-mode evaluation.
D3762-24 explicitly is not a quantitative fracture-strength method.
The standard permits considering other materials with thickness/rigidity considerations, but S0 cannot authenticate or approve that suitability review.
An unrecognized edition cannot inherit the currently pinned D1002-26 scope.
Protocol identity alone is insufficient without a well-formed protocol digest reference.
The raw-data artifact digest reference is absent.
Duplicated specimen identities prevent independent specimen accounting.
The protocol supports a wettability observation only.
Contact angle is not a direct bond-strength measurement.
An ISO 4587 lap-shear endpoint does not establish fatigue life.
A model score without a registered test method cannot be promoted into a physical measurement claim.
The geometry does not match the registered standard single-lap method.
The raw-data digest reference does not have the required lowercase SHA-256 shape.
Active D3163-01R23 covers comparative single-lap shear tests for rigid plastic adherends.
A rigid-plastic single-lap result does not become a structural design allowable.
D3163 is scoped to rigid plastic adherends, not metal-to-metal.
An older reaffirmation does not inherit the active D3163-01R23 registry entry.
D5868 covers comparative lap-shear measurement for FRP-to-FRP joints.
D5868 covers FRP joined to metals as well as FRP-to-FRP.
D5868 does not cover a metal-to-metal-only adherend pair.
An FRP single-lap apparent shear value is not a structural design allowable.
D2093 is a plastic surface-preparation practice, not an adhesive strength test.
A surface-preparation practice cannot be promoted into bond-strength evidence.
D1151 defines continuous moisture/temperature exposure conditions; a separate strength test measures retained-strength response.
A conditioning practice and finite exposure duration do not establish calendar service life.
D1183 defines cyclic accelerated laboratory-aging exposures, not field-life equivalence.
Cyclic accelerated exposure does not itself predict calendar service lifetime.
D4896 is a guide for safe and appropriate interpretation of single-lap strength results.
D4896 warns against using small single-lap strength values as structural design allowables.
The evidence kind cannot relabel a test method as a preparation practice.
D5868 is a single-lap FRP method; a double-lap geometry is outside the registered method scope.
D1151 defines conditioning conditions; the retained-strength measurement must be supplied by a separate strength-test method.
Exact 2026 thick-adherend method and aluminum specimen support adhesive shear stress-strain characterization only.
D5656 characterizes adhesive shear response, not adhesion to a particular substrate.
Constitutive response cannot be promoted to joint bond strength.
D5656 does not produce the D3163/D5868 apparent single-lap shear endpoint.
The 2026 standard does not assume validity for non-aluminum adherends.
Historical or unrecognized D5656 editions do not inherit the current D5656/D5656M-26 registration.
A thick-adherend test method cannot be relabeled as an environmental conditioning practice.
D5656's thick-adherend geometry cannot be replaced by an ordinary single-lap geometry.
D5573 supports descriptive classification of failure modes for its scoped SMC FRP joint family.
D5573 expressly does not determine whether a specific failure mode is acceptable.
A failure-mode classification practice is not a lap-shear strength test.
General FRP applicability outside the specified SMC family needs a separately reviewed scope bridge.
A failure-mode classification practice cannot be presented as a measurement test method.
The previous reaffirmation does not inherit the active D5573-99R19 registration.
D882-26 supports tensile observations for plastic films and thin sheeting below 1.0 mm.
D882-26 scope is below 1.0 mm; thicker material requires the appropriate separate method.
A tensile observation does not establish product safety or universal substrate integrity.
ISO 15106-5:2015 is a pressure-sensor method for water-vapour transmission rate of plastic films, sheeting and multilayer structures.
ISO 15105-2:2025 covers equal-pressure gas-transmission measurement for plastic film, sheeting, laminates, co-extruded and flexible coated materials.
The withdrawn 2003 edition does not inherit the exact 2025 registration.
A transmission measurement method cannot be relabeled as a conditioning practice.
The registered D15105-2-2025 profile is equal-pressure; a different method geometry is not admitted by this entry.
A gas-transmission rate observation does not independently establish package shelf life.
